title: University Of Michigan Slapped With Lawsuit By Ticket Seller For $2 Million After School Allegedly Locks Accounts | The Daily Caller
text:
The University of Michigan has been hit with a lawsuit by a season ticket holder following the college allegedly locking his accounts where he re-sold tickets.
The owner of the scalping service Maxim Tickets, Kevin Brick, has been in the business for the last 20 years where he buys Michigan football tickets with the intention of putting them back on sale. Per the lawsuit, Brick ran a total of 164 accounts and claims that he’s donated millions to Michigan in order to get Priority Points benefits connected to choice seating options. (RELATED: Ohio State Senator Introduces Absolutely Fantastic College Football Bill That All Of America Needs To Get Behind)
The school installed a new policy in 2023 that prohibits individuals from purchasing tickets just to put them back on the market to make a profit. Each person is also limited to just eight tickets, according to reports.
“Multiple accounts may not be used to circumvent or exceed published ticket limits,” reads the policy as of publication. “We reserve the right to any or all orders and tickets, in addition to prohibiting your ticket purchase abilities, without notice, if you exceed or attempt to exceed, the posted ticket limits.”
A scalper who spent decades flipping tickets to Michigan football games filed a massive lawsuit after the school cracked down on the practice

Brick claims that Michigan allegedly locking his accounts cost him lost revenue of $2.5 million.
“Despite UM’s longstanding policy of allowing resale and transfer of football season tickets, it unilaterally changed its terms and conditions without (our) consent or knowledge in (and) around 2023,” alleges the lawsuit.
MLive reports that Brick is looking for damages of $2 million.
